questions.q: Find the arc length of $y = \frac{2}{3}x^{3/2}$ from $x=0$ to $x=3$.
Set up (do not evaluate) the arc length integral for $y = \sin x$ on $[0, \pi]$.
Evaluate $\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^2}\,dx$, or state that it diverges.
Evaluate $\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x}\,dx$, or state that it diverges.
Find the arc length of the line $y=3x+1$ from $x=0$ to $x=4$, and verify your answer using the distance formula.
Set up (do not evaluate) the arc length integral for $y=\ln x$ on $[1,e]$.
Evaluate $\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^{1.5}}\,dx$, or state that it diverges.
Evaluate $\int_{-\infty}^0 e^x\,dx$, or state that it diverges.
For $\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^p}\,dx$, state the condition on $p$ for convergence, and explain why using the antiderivative $\frac{x^{1-p}}{1-p}$ (for $p\neq1$).
questions.answer: Converges when $p>1$. As $b\to\infty$, $b^{1-p}\to0$ only when $1-p<0$, i.e. $p>1$; otherwise the limit is infinite (or, for $p=1$, the antiderivative is $\ln x$, which also diverges).

questions.q: Use the $p$-integral result to quickly determine whether $\int_1^\infty \frac{1}{x^{0.9}}\,dx$ converges.

sections.heading: Improper integrals with infinite discontinuities inside the interval

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_0^2 \frac{1}{(x-1)^2}\,dx$, or explain why it diverges (note the integrand is undefined at $x=1$, inside the interval).
questions.answer: Split at $x=1$: $\int_0^1\frac{1}{(x-1)^2}dx + \int_1^2\frac{1}{(x-1)^2}dx$. Near $x=1$ from either side, $\lim_{b\to1}\left[-\frac{1}{x-1}\right]$ blows up to $\pm\infty$: both pieces diverge, so the full integral diverges.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{1}{x^{1/3}}\,dx$ (an odd function with a discontinuity at $x=0$), splitting at $x=0$.
questions.answer: By symmetry (odd integrand), $\int_{-1}^0 x^{-1/3}dx = -\int_0^1 x^{-1/3}dx$ (each piece converges since $p=\frac{1}{3}<1$ for this type of integrand near a finite discontinuity). The two pieces cancel: the integral equals $0$.
